--- title: "Descriptive Statistics" subtitle: "Distribution · temporal coverage · outliers · zero-inflation per variable" date: last-modified --- ## Overview This page provides variable-level diagnostics for all 175 numeric variables in the PDET panel (170 municipalities, 2000--2025). ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## How to read the diagnostic flags Each category tab shows four things: 1. **Summary statistics table** -- searchable table with N, % missing, % zero, mean, median, SD, skewness, municipality coverage, and year range. The `is_static` column marks variables with zero within-municipality variation across years (these cannot be used in fixed-effects models). 2. **Diagnostic flags** -- automatic alerts for: - *Zero-inflated (>50% zeros):* Most observations are zero; the variable measures rare events. Consider a binary indicator or hurdle model. - *High missingness (>50% NA):* The variable covers less than half the panel. Missingness is likely MAR (conditional on year or department) -- see the Data Audit page. - *Highly skewed (|skew| > 3):* Distribution has a very long right tail. Log(1 + x) transformation strongly recommended before regression. - *Static (no within-muni variation):* Value is identical across all years for each municipality. Cannot be used as outcome in panel FE models; useful only as cross-sectional moderator. - *Low coverage (<100 munis):* Fewer than 100 of 170 PDET municipalities have any data. - *Short time span (<10 years):* Limited temporal coverage. 3. **Distributions** -- histograms for each variable. Zero-inflated variables will show a large spike at zero. Skewed variables will have long right tails. 4. **Temporal trends** -- median value across municipalities by year. Dot size = number of municipalities with data that year. Flat lines = static variables. The 2016 vertical line (where shown) marks the Peace Agreement. ::: ::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"} ## Variables flagged for exclusion or recoding Based on diagnostics, the following variables should be **dropped or recoded** before modeling: - `P_investment_total_cop__art`, `P_n_projects_completed__art`, `P_n_pilars_covered__art` -- all zeros, failed extraction - `P_impl_ceasefire_disarmament__art`, `P_impl_communication__art` -- >99% NA, near-zero/constant variance - `S_n_cadastral_managers__igac` -- constant = 1, zero variance - `G_land_cover_share__prio` -- near-constant (mean = 0.97), negligible variation - `J_n_restitution_sentences__urt` -- constant = 1 for all observed rows, likely misspecified; verify source - `V_homicides_q025__jep`, `V_homicides_q975__jep` -- redundant with mean (r ~ 1) - `S_gdp_percapita_constant__dnp` -- only 5 years (2005-2009) - `S_poverty_headcount__dnp` -- single year (2005), use as baseline control only All other variables with >50% NA or high skew are usable with appropriate transformation and available-case estimation. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} overview <- desc_table |> dplyr::group_by(Category = cat_labels[category]) |> dplyr::summarise( `N vars` = dplyr::n(), `Median % NA` = round(median(pct_na), 1), `Median % zero` = round(median(pct_zero, na.rm = TRUE), 1), `N static` = sum(is_static, na.rm = TRUE), `N high-skew` = sum(abs(skewness) > 3, na.rm = TRUE), `Year range` = paste0(min(year_min, na.rm = TRUE), "–", max(year_max, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop" ) DT::datatable(overview, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 10), caption = "Category-level summary") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

**Short time span (<10 years):** population_grid #### Distributions ![](descriptives_files/figure-html/desc-geo-1.png){width=1050} #### Temporal Trends (median across municipalities) ![](descriptives_files/figure-html/desc-geo-2.png){width=1050} ::: --- ## Cross-Category Correlation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Pick one representative variable per source for a manageable heatmap rep_vars <- desc_table |> dplyr::group_by(source) |> dplyr::slice_max(n_obs, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> dplyr::pull(variable) if (length(rep_vars) >= 3) { cor_data <- panel |> dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(rep_vars)) cor_mat <- cor(cor_data, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "spearman") # Clean names for display rownames(cor_mat) <- gsub("__.*", "", gsub("^[VPJSG]_", "", rownames(cor_mat))) colnames(cor_mat) <- gsub("__.*", "", gsub("^[VPJSG]_", "", colnames(cor_mat))) cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) |> dplyr::rename(var1 = Var1, var2 = Var2, rho = Freq) ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = var1, y = var2, fill = rho)) + geom_tile(color = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(abs(rho) > 0.3, sprintf("%.2f", rho), "")), size = 2) + scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Spearman rho") + theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme( axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), panel.grid = element_blank() ) + labs(title = "Cross-source Spearman correlations (one variable per source)", x = NULL, y = NULL) } ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](descriptives_files/figure-html/correlation-heatmap-1.png){width=1050} ::: :::
